purpose: Claude-family successor of generator-multimodel-v1. The v1 Claude rows were harness-limited in three ways found by an independent audit of the stored claude-sonnet-5-5 cells: (1) arm A could not verify its output (port conflict), (2) arm C was only a minimal treatment because the skill was staged in a temporary directory with slash commands disabled, (3) the engine kept only the first 400 characters of each command, so long scanner invocations were missed. This protocol keeps the same 36 cells per model and changes only what the audit identified, records what each call actually did from the raw stream-json (parent and subagents), reports the primary metric in the way it is measured, adds secondary refactor classes and a cost endpoint, and pre-registers a pooled analysis.
v1_claude_rows_status: harness-limited descriptive. The v1 Claude results are neither replaced, corrected nor re-read as quality differences by this protocol; claude-sonnet-5-5 is re-run (see sonnet_rule).

load.rule: Inherited wait: a cell waits (60 s steps, at most 1800 s) while the 1-minute load average is above 40, then starts regardless. The load average is recorded at the start of every cell. A cell whose load_at_start is above 40 is FLAGGED, never dropped; the load_clean view recomputes the labels without flagged cells as a sensitivity.

execution_identity.note: v1 ran Claude Code 2.1.299. A newer CLI is accepted (the floor is checked with `claude --version`, which is not a model call) and is recorded per model in final.json; a resume with a different CLI string is refused by the inherited v1 loop, so finish a model before upgrading. Model ids are what the local CLI accepted in the v1 probe of 2026-10-14; they are provenance, not attestation.

roster_note: The roster is the four Claude models of v1. Run order puts sonnet first (it carries the pre-freeze live checks), then the smaller model, then the two larger ones. The cross-model count rule needs all four models to be complete and evaluable (min_models 4); the pooled analysis needs only two. Every model is run regardless of what its v1 campaign showed; no model is excluded by an entry rule because arm A fidelity is directly observable in the Claude stream (subagent tool calls are in the parent stream) and is reported, not used to drop models.
sonnet_rule: claude-sonnet-5-5 already has v1 data and is re-run under v2 anyway. Reason: in v1 its arm A parent could never verify its own output (the parent's single `playwright test` run failed with 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health is already used' before any test started in 12 of 12 A cells, because the MCP session of the official generator keeps the app server alive on the configured port) and its arm C was a minimal treatment (SKILL.md read 12/12, but no reference file read through the Read tool 0/12, no preflight 0/12, no browser exploration 0/12, scan.sh in 6/12 cells, an independent review in 1/12, self-reported complete 0/12, about 55 s per cell, with the skill staged in a temporary directory and `--disable-slash-commands` set, so the model had to read files by hand). Rule: a v2 model is a v2 model; its v1 cells are never merged into v2 cells, views, N or the pooled analysis, and `summary --v1-dir` only lists the v1 label beside the v2 rows, marked as the frozen v1 harness. Sonnet also runs the pre-freeze live checks (init-check, preflight) because it is the one model whose v1 transcripts the extractors were tested on; those calls are never data.

port_fix.diagnosis: The official generator's MCP session keeps the app server of the configured port alive (generator_setup_page pauses the seed test with its webServer running). The benchmark config declares reuseExistingServer false with one port, so the parent's later `playwright test` fails before any test starts. Scoring must keep reuseExistingServer false and a clean environment, because a leftover server would serve the original app to a mutant run.
port_fix.mechanism:
split-port: app.mjs `const PORT =

;` becomes `Number(process.env.E2E_APP_PORT ??

)`; the config's baseURL and webServer url become template strings with the same default. With the variable unset (the parent, `node app.mjs`, `playwright test`) behaviour is byte-for-byte the case's. The MCP server receives E2E_APP_PORT =

+ 20000 through its own mcp-config file.
port_fix.fallback: reuse (flip reuseExistingServer to true in the generation project) is implemented but not selected: the parent's runs would then share a dirty app instance with the MCP session, and a spec repaired against that state can fail on the fresh scoring app. Choose it only if the live check shows that the MCP server does not propagate its env to the app server.
port_fix.scoring_unchanged: The scoring path (engine.evaluate_specs, engine.stage on the case directory, the secondary refactor runs) is not patched. The offline test stages every task through engine.stage and shows reuseExistingServer false and no E2E_APP_PORT, shows the transform is applied only inside the cell builder, and shows the arms' parent environment never carries the variable.
port_fix.runtime_guard: If a parent `playwright test` result in arm A still reports 'is already used' and the model did not start a server itself, the call is an infrastructure error (harness_port_conflict), retried by the inherited loop and counted toward the three-in-a-row stop. A genuine model-caused conflict (the model ran `node app.mjs` itself) is not an infrastructure error.
port_fix.unverified: That Claude Code passes the mcp-config env to the MCP server process and that the Playwright MCP server's test run inherits it is NOT verified offline; see live_checks.

skills.install: Copied from the repository `skills/<name>/` (without `evals/`) to `<project>/.claude/skills/<name>/` before the baseline commit; the staged tree is compared with the repository tree; the repository skills tree is bound by the v1 bindings.
skills.bundled_allowed_note: Skills that Claude Code itself bundles may be listed by a real init event next to the project skills. The list is empty until `init-check` has been run on the host; its output (`suggest_bundled_allowed`) is pasted here BEFORE the freeze. Any other extra skill, a prefixed plugin skill, or a missing intended skill is an infrastructure error.
skills.permissions: arms B and C: `--tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash,Write,Edit,Agent,Skill` and `--allowedTools ...,Skill(<intended name>)` for each intended skill only; arm A has no Skill tool.
skills.trust_note: The skills' own SKILL.md files classify a script as skill-owned only when its real path lies outside the target worktree. A project skill sits inside the worktree, so the prompts grant the exact script commands as per-row approvals. This is a deliberate harness statement, listed as an owner decision.

isolation_contract.checked_on: every system/init event of every call
isolation_contract.arm_A: skills [] ; slash_commands [] ; agents include playwright-test-generator ; mcp_servers exactly {playwright-test: connected} ; tools: no Write, Edit, NotebookEdit, WebFetch, WebSearch, Skill ; the generator_setup_page and generator_write_test MCP tools present
isolation_contract.arms_B_C: skills = intended + bundled_allowed ; no playwright-test-* agents ; no MCP servers or mcp__ tools ; no web tools ; Write, Edit and Skill present
isolation_contract.all_arms: model equals the requested id (bracket suffix ignored) ; cwd is the cell project ; every plugin is builtin ; one violation anywhere is an infrastructure error
isolation_contract.slash_commands_B_C: recorded, not enforced (the real list is unknown until the init-check)

transports.claude: generator_claude_multimodel_adapter_v2.py: the frozen v1 argv with the minimum changes. Arm A: `--mcp-config` points to a copy of `.mcp.json` outside the project with the port-split env; settings deny list extended with the running checkout. Arms B and C: `--disable-slash-commands` removed, `--setting-sources project`, tools and allowed tools extended with the Skill tool for the intended skills. Subagents are pinned to the matrix model through CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL as in v1; E2E_APP_PORT is removed from the call environment. Strict fidelity: only completed MCP calls count; the full final message is kept; modelUsage is cross-checked against the stream.
transports.claude_official_arm: Unchanged from v1: `npx --no-install playwright init-agents --loop=claude`, four files digest-checked against the v1 protocol, then the single `model: sonnet` line replaced by `model: inherit` (v1 code, v1 digests).
transports.argv_diff_test: the offline test diffs the v2 argv of every arm against the frozen adapter's and asserts exactly these differences

prompt_lines.B: asks for the installed `e2e-reviewer` skill by name, states the scope (untracked files under tests/) and the per-row scanner approval; the 'Then FIX every finding...' paragraph is the v1 text unchanged
prompt_lines.C: asks for the installed `playwright-test-generator` skill by name, states the per-row approval of the skills' scripts in `.claude/skills/` and the scratch-file sentence also used by the Codex successor
prompt_lines.binding: sha256 of each line is bound in the freeze

fidelity.source: the raw stream-json of each call, parent and subagent tool_use blocks alike (Claude streams include subagent events with parent_tool_use_id)
fidelity.recomputed: analyze recomputes every record from the stored transcript, so an extractor fix needs no rerun; the run-time record is only a fallback

definitions.generator_skill_loaded: a Skill tool call naming playwright-test-generator, or a Read-tool or Bash read-verb (cat, sed, head, tail, grep ...) of its SKILL.md
definitions.refs_read_any: any of the nine sibling reference files read through the Read tool OR through a Bash read verb (cat, sed, head, tail, grep, rg ...); the path must name the playwright-test-generator directory, start with a shell variable, or resolve through a `cd` into that directory (the working directory is tracked across Bash calls of one agent); a glob (`*.md`, `*`) in that directory counts as all nine. A file name that only appears in ls, echo or a here-document is a mention and is recorded separately (generator_refs_mentioned). Both access paths are recorded separately
definitions.hot_refs_read_2plus: at least two of best-practices.md, scenario-design.md, code-rules.md, verification-rules.md
definitions.preflight: the skill-owned run-preflight-target.sh (or preflight_target.py) EXECUTED as the program or as the script of a shell or interpreter in a simple command; a mention (cat, ls, echo, grep) is recorded as preflight_mentions only
definitions.exploration: EXECUTED playwright cli, playwright-cli, agent-browser or run-raw-aria-snapshot, or an MCP browser tool call; mentions are recorded as exploration_mentions
definitions.scan_sh: scan.sh EXECUTED: the program, or the script of bash, sh, zsh, dash, ksh or an interpreter, in a simple command (after assignments and wrappers such as env, timeout, npx), on the full command (no truncation), including inside `bash -c '...'`. `bash -n`, cat, ls, grep, echo and here-document text do not count; the looser 'scan.sh appears in the command' count is recorded as scan_sh_mentions
definitions.baseline_run: an EXECUTED `playwright test` (the program is playwright with the argument test, also via npx, pnpm exec, yarn, node ... or a path ending in /playwright) before the first spec Write or Edit
definitions.targeted_run: an EXECUTED `playwright test` after the first spec Write or Edit; playwright_test_mentions records the looser text match
definitions.independent_review: an Agent spawn after the first spec write whose description or prompt NAMES e2e-reviewer or the V6 gate (or whose subagent type names a reviewer), or an e2e-reviewer Skill call made by a subagent after that write. A spawn that only contains the word 'review' is recorded as review_mentions_after_write and does not count
definitions.port_conflict: a tool_result of the parent's `playwright test` containing 'is already used' / EADDRINUSE

treatment.invoked: A: generator_setup_page or generator_write_test called ; B: reviewer skill loaded ; C: generator skill loaded
treatment.treated: A: generator_setup_page AND generator_write_test called (the child's calls are in the stream) ; B: reviewer skill loaded AND scan.sh AND a playwright test run ; C: generator skill loaded AND at least two hot reference files AND scan.sh AND a targeted run AND an independent review agent
treatment.note: Defined before any v2 data exists, from the SKILL.md steps. v1 treatment rates differ strongly by model (gpt-5.5 arm C: all key steps in 10 of 12 cells, gpt-6-sol 5 of 12, claude-sonnet-5-5 0 of 12 on the audit's definition), so no per-model contrast is read without the fidelity table and the as-treated view.

fidelity.spec_headers_are_not_evidence: the '// spec:' and '// seed:' headers are not evidence of generator use; only tool calls are
fidelity.executed_vs_mentioned: Every step above is counted only when the command is executed. The pre-registered classifier is a quote-aware split of the Bash command into simple commands (separators ; newline && || | & ( ) and command substitution), with here-document bodies removed, assignments and transparent wrappers skipped, and `bash -c` text parsed recursively. It is not a full shell: a command hidden in a variable, a `for` list, an alias or a script file the model wrote is not seen (undercount). The looser mention counts are kept as separate fields beside each step. Negative controls (cat, ls, echo, bash -n, here-document text, a generic 'review' spawn) are unit-tested.
fidelity.unintended_skills: Every Skill tool call outside the arm's intended skills, and every Skill call whose tool_result is an error (a denied or failed call), is recorded per cell (unintended_skill_calls, skill_call_errors) and counted in the fidelity table. Arms B and C list Claude Code's bundled skills in their context while arm A lists none (an asymmetry in context, not only in tools); whether a bundled skill was attempted is visible in these fields.

strict_completion.rule: A generator_* or browser_* call of the playwright-test server counts only when it COMPLETED: its tool_result is present and not flagged is_error. Attempted-but-failed, denied or unanswered calls are recorded as *_attempted and mcp_tools_denied and never raise a step or the treated flag.
strict_completion.classes_arm_a: official-tool (a completed generator_* or browser_* call, parent or subagent), manual-follow (delivered, calls refused, no positive), unverified (delivered, no positive), blocked (not delivered, no positive), aborted. The same class names as the Codex v3 harness; B cells carry their source A cell's class (source_fidelity_class).
strict_completion.minimal_use: `minimal_generator_use` marks an official-tool cell without any completed browser call; `browser_mutating_calls` counts the mutating ones. The class proves the official surface was touched, not that the exploration loop ran.
strict_completion.mcp_artifacts: .playwright-mcp/ snapshot files are tool output: kept as the count mcp_artifact_files, not listed under out_of_scope_writes.
strict_completion.cost_cross_check: modelUsage is compared with the per-message usage visible in the stream (subagent messages included); a session total below that lower bound sets cost_covers_stream false for the cell and is counted in the cost and fidelity tables.

views.itt: all 36 cells as run; aborted cells score 0 as in v1. The decision view and the first pooled view.
views.invoked: sensitivity: A/B/C cells with the invoked flag; a B cell needs its own flag and its source A cell's; aborted cells removed
views.as_treated: sensitivity: cells with the treated flag (B: own and source A); aborted cells removed. A per-protocol analysis: treatment is a post-randomization variable that may correlate with outcome
views.load_clean: sensitivity: itt without aborted cells and without cells started above load 40 (a B cell goes with a flagged source A cell)
views.mapping_to_codex_v2: this itt = the Codex successor's itt ; this as_treated = the Codex successor's as_treated view (every arm gated on observed treatment: A official-tool, B reviewed an official-tool cell and ran its reviewer steps, C core steps). The Codex successor's `primary` view is NOT an as-treated analogue (it gates arm A, and B through its source, on the official-tool class and leaves every arm C cell ungated); the combined table lists it separately as itt/primary.
views.discordance: The summary prints, per contrast, the views whose cross-model verdict differs from itt's and, per model, the views whose label differs from itt's. A discordant view is reported as discordance; the itt verdict is not replaced by it.

classes.text_label: visible text and accessible names reworded (field labels, button names, status copy, aria-labels; the h1 is left alone because the case's smoke spec asserts it); ids, classes, roles and structure unchanged; every new text avoids the old text as a substring. Corresponds to R-TEXT in the Codex successor's specification
classes.structure: extra wrappers and regrouped children; no existing id or class removed or changed, roles, accessible names and visible text unchanged. Corresponds to R-STRUCT in the Codex successor's specification

secondary_refactors.primary_unchanged: the primary refactor (id/class renames plus wrappers, from the v3 truth files) is untouched and remains the primary metric
secondary_refactors.scoring: a cell scores 1 for a class iff it is clean 3/3 on the original app and its specs pass on the app with the class's edits applied (score-secondary, same staging as scoring); secondary only, never in a decision rule
secondary_refactors.validation: static only offline (markers, node --check, static markup census); `validate-refactors --allow-local` on the host before the freeze checks, for every task, that the ARIA snapshot is identical before and after the structure class and changes under the text class, and that the case's existing smoke spec passes on both variants

metrics.primary: markup-refactor survival (1 only if clean 3/3 and the refactor passes), mean over the 2 repetitions per task
metrics.primary_reading: Reported as what it measures. In the audit of stored v1 cells, a clean spec that names a pre-refactor #id or .class selector failed the refactor in 23 of 23 cells and a clean spec that names none passed it in all 62; refactor survival is therefore, to a first approximation, 'the clean spec names no renamed id or class'. The decomposition table reports, per arm, clean cells by that property and the survival of each group, plus the clean-conditional survival. The audit's counts were not re-derived here except on the stored sonnet cells, and the split is true by construction (a spec that names a renamed id or class fails the refactor), so it explains the metric and is not independent evidence. The selector reader looks only at selector literals (the first argument of locator, $, $$, querySelector, click, fill and similar calls, or a literal that as a whole is a CSS selector), ignores `${...}` interpolations, and does not count a substring attribute selector that survives the rename; it was refined on the stored v1 sonnet cells, which makes its reproduction of the audit's split in-sample. A dynamic-selector hint is stored per cell and counted among the clean cells naming none.
reported_per_model_and_arm: refactor survival, clean-conditional survival, text_label and structure secondary survival
effective fault kill and raw kill rate
clean 3/3 rate, scanner P0 and P1/P2
delivered, unavailable, timeout and aborted cells
home-directory paths touched outside the work directory

decision.no_p_values: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. No significance claim and no PASS/FAIL verdict. Every p-value and interval printed by the tools is descriptive unless the owner approves inference in writing before any v2 data is scored.
decision.per_model_label: v1's rule restated and applied to the cells of a view: EVALUABLE only if both arms have at least 6 delivered spec files in the view and share at least 5 tasks; then 'suggestive: X better' if X's per-task refactor survival is higher in at least 5 of 6 tasks and X's clean-3/3 rate, effective fault kill, scanner P0 and scanner P1/P2 (per cell) are not worse; otherwise 'nothing'. Ties and 3-3 splits are 'nothing'. Kept for continuity with v1 and the Codex successor; it is NOT the main analysis (see pooled_analysis): its per-model power for a pilot-sized effect is about 23%.

cross_model.scope: Claude family only; decided on the itt view; the other views are sensitivities
cross_model.rule: Per contrast, N = complete models (36 scored cells, at most 3 aborted) for which the contrast is evaluable in the view. N < 4: 'not evaluable'. Otherwise 'consistent: X better in k of N models' only if at least max(2, ceil(N/3)) models carry 'suggestive: X better' and none carries the opposite label; else 'not consistent'. Same constants as the Codex successor (which adds a two-lineage clause that does not apply to a single generation). With four models the threshold is 2 agreeing models: a weak bar worded as a count, not a replication. v1's ceil(2N/3) rule had about 4% power at most; 'not consistent' is the expected outcome even for a real effect.
cross_model.justification: see power_simulation and the README; the rule is kept so that the two families are read with the same count rule

cost_endpoints.co_primary: Cost is read next to quality, never alone: (1) refactor survivors per 100k processed tokens ('quality per 100k tokens'), (2) pipeline seconds (mean per cell and per survivor), both reported in every view's cost table. Same definition as the Codex successor.
cost_endpoints.processed_tokens: uncached input + cache write + output, parent and subagents together (modelUsage inputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens + outputTokens). Cache reads are excluded from the co-primary denominator and reported separately; the same ratio with cache reads added is printed as a sensitivity (quality_per_100k_total).
cost_endpoints.pipeline: Arm A and arm C: the call itself. Arm B: its source arm A cell plus the reviewer call (the reviewer pass costs the generation it reviews). A pipeline is complete only if every call in it has a modelUsage record.
cost_endpoints.ratio_of_sums: survivors (sum of refactor_score) in the cells with token records divided by the sum of their tokens (not a mean of per-cell ratios); a cell with no token record at all is counted and excluded
also_reported: uncached input, cache write, cache read and output separately (own call)
USD from modelUsage (own and pipeline) and quality per USD
cells whose modelUsage names another model
whether the modelUsage cost sum equals total_cost_usd
cost_endpoints.token_source: the last result event's modelUsage, which is cumulative for the session and includes subagents (the v1 'usage' field is the last turn only)
cost_endpoints.comparability: Claude and Codex tokens are not comparable (tokenizers, caching, loops); Codex child-agent tokens are missing from its parent stream unless its rollouts are parsed
cost_endpoints.pooled_use: the pooled analysis may include quality_per_100k_processed, quality_per_100k_total and pipeline_seconds as additional metrics, descriptive like the rest
cost_endpoints.timeouts: A call killed at the wall-clock limit has no result event, so no modelUsage. Its tokens are taken as a LOWER BOUND from the assistant usage fields of the stream (parent and subagents, one entry per message id; streamed output counts are partial, USD unknown and counted as 0) and the cell stays in the quality-per-token ratio, flagged lower_bound. This keeps an arm with more timeouts from looking cheaper per survivor. The cost table also reports, per arm, the number of timeouts, the seconds they consumed and the cells with lower-bound tokens; a timed-out cell with no assistant message has no record and is excluded.

pooled_analysis.written: before any successor data is scored; bound in the freeze through this file
pooled_analysis.motivation: The frozen v1 per-model sign rule (same sign in at least 5 of 6 tasks) has about 23% power per model for a pilot-sized effect and the cross-model rule at most about 4% in the v1 line (this protocol's own simulation is in power_simulation). A pooled analysis that uses the size of the effect, with models and tasks as clusters, is the pre-registered complement. It does not replace the rule and issues no verdict.
pooled_analysis.metrics_note: refactor_score (the headline metric) is the primary metric. refactor_score, clean and effective_fault_kill are the metrics the Codex successor also pools under the same names; the others are Claude-side additions (clean-conditional survival, the two secondary refactor classes, the two cost endpoints). Every metric is reported in both views.
pooled_analysis.pool: Complete models whose contrast is evaluable in the view (the cross-model rule's own eligibility); incomplete models are excluded, as in the rule.
pooled_analysis.unit: Model-by-task: per task the mean metric of arm X cells minus that of arm Y cells in the view, for tasks where both arms have a value; repetitions are averaged inside a task.
pooled_analysis.estimate: Unweighted mean over models of each model's unweighted mean over its tasks (every model counts once, regardless of how many cells its view keeps).
pooled_analysis.sign_flip: Exact two-sided sign-flip test over models: all 2^N sign patterns of the N model effects, p = share of patterns whose absolute mean reaches the observed one. The smallest attainable p is 2/2^N: 0.125 at N = 4 (it can never reach 0.05 for the four Claude models), 0.03125 at N = 6, 0.0020 at N = 10; it is printed beside every p.

cluster_bootstrap.resampling: crossed: models drawn with replacement and tasks drawn with replacement, the estimate recomputed on the resampled grid, percentile interval; a draw with no value is skipped and counted. With 4 to 6 models and 6 tasks this interval is shown as a spread, not a guarantee (in this protocol's null simulation its lower bound exceeded zero in at most about 1% of replicates).

pooled_analysis.robustness: per-model effects, models positive and negative, family and lineage means, per-task profile across models, leave-one-model-out estimates.

owner_approval.note: Every number of this section carries the label 'descriptive (inference not approved)'. Quoting the sign-flip p-value or the bootstrap interval as evidence requires the owner to set inference to true in a written addendum bound before the v2 results are read; the computation does not change.

pooled_analysis.reporting: summary (Pooled analysis section) and <root>/summary.json. No verdict wording.
pooled_analysis.view_mapping_to_codex_successor: this itt = its itt; this as_treated = its as_treated (both gate every arm on observed treatment). Its `primary` view gates only arm A (and B through its source) and leaves arm C ungated, so it is paired with this itt as a separately labelled analogue only. Here itt is the primary view because treatment is directly observed and the as-treated view is a per-protocol sensitivity.
pooled_analysis.combination_with_codex: `summary --codex-dir <v2-codex output root>` pools the model effects of both families with each model one unit (up to ten models) from the cells of the Codex results, in the pairs itt/itt, as_treated/as_treated and itt/primary (the last one a separately labelled analogue), for refactor_score, clean and effective_fault_kill, prints the family and lineage means beside the pooled estimate, and claims no joint verdict. Host, loop and transport (container versus host) differences remain confounded with family.
pooled_analysis.successor_alignment: Same unit, estimate, exact sign-flip, crossed cluster bootstrap (10000 replicates, seed 20261016, level 0.95, same seeding and percentile rule) and owner flags as the Codex successor; tested against the Codex pooled module when it is present.

aborted_cell_rule: An aborted cell is an infrastructure outcome: an error after the inherited in-call retry, a usage or rate limit, an isolation-contract violation, a harness port conflict, a disk floor, or arm A setup UNAVAILABLE (marked infrastructure_error so that the inherited retry and stop rules apply). A timeout and an empty source for arm B are not aborts. Aborted cells are retried by later resumes at most twice, score 0 in itt and leave the other views; more than 3 aborted cells make a model incomplete; three infrastructure-error cells in a row stop the campaign and a usage or rate limit stops it at once.

availability_signals: fidelity record: every step counter, the Read-tool and Bash access paths, subagent census and subagent_stats
setup status, installed skill digests, port-fix summary
aborted flag and the error text of every attempt
cost: modelUsage by model with the four token kinds
total_cost_usd and whether the modelUsage sum matches it
host: host_pressure at the start of the cell: 1-minute load, swap used and total in MB

schedule: Each model runs the same 36 cells in the frozen v1 order (24 A and C cells shuffled by seed, then 12 B cells shuffled by seed+1, so B follows the A cell it reviews). One call at a time across the campaign; a v2 driver holds a campaign lock file, refuses to start while another multimodel driver process exists, and uses scoring and staging ports offset by 6000 from v1's (v1 uses 5300+ for scoring and 6300+/6700+ for staging, so v2-claude uses 11300+ and 12300+/12700+; the arm A MCP server adds 20000; there is no occupancy check, so make sure nothing else listens there).
combination_with_v1: No v1 cell is merged into v2. `summary --v1-dir` lists the v1 Claude labels beside the v2 labels, marked as the frozen v1 harness. v1's own cross-model rule and verdict are not recomputed.
stop_rules: One model call at a time within this campaign (workers 1); the Codex campaign may run beside it (see coexistence). Load pause at 1-min load average > 40 (up to 1800 s per wait).
Stop when free disk on the work volume is below 4 GiB (4294967296 bytes), before every call; resume with `drive --allow-live`.
Stop on a usage or rate limit or any digest drift.

An isolation-contract violation is treated as systematic: the call is an infrastructure error flagged fatal, the campaign stops after that single call (no second attempt, no three-in-a-row wait) and the row is kept; resume retries it after the cause is fixed. The stop message of the inherited loop says 'usage/rate limit'; the row's attempt error names the violation.
An infrastructure-error cell is retried at most twice by later resumes; three consecutive infrastructure-error cells stop the campaign. A harness port conflict counts as an infrastructure error.

Never edit this protocol, the runner, the adapter, refactors.json or freeze.json after the first scheduled call; a change needs a successor protocol. The README may only grow below its Results heading.

Pre-freeze path: run init-check and preflight, paste the bundled-skill list into skills.bundled_allowed, run validate-refactors, record the power table, then freeze. Delete freeze.json and refreeze only before the first scheduled call.

`drive` refuses unless an init-check result exists for the CLI build installed now, with all three arms present and every stored init event passing the isolation contract under the current skills.bundled_allowed. A CLI upgrade after init-check voids the check.

The campaign guard (`guard`, run by every live verb and by score, score-secondary and validate-refactors) refuses to start only for a TRUE conflict: another Claude-family driver, a Zeppelin-using driver, an overlapping output root, a host port range that overlaps this campaign's ranges or a socket already listening inside them, or an unclassified run-generator driver. A running Codex container driver is not a conflict.
live_checks: init-check (one cheap call per arm): confirms that the real project skills are listed in a real init event, which bundled skills appear next to them, that arm A lists none and has no Skill tool, and that the verifier passes; fill skills.bundled_allowed from its output

preflight on v2-01 for arm A: the parent's `playwright test` after generator_write_test must NOT report 'is already used' (the port split); and that mcp-config env reaches the MCP server's app process
preflight for arms B and C: the Skill tool call, the `Skill(<name>)` allow rules, the skill scripts' execution under the granted approvals, and the second reference-read path
validate-refactors --allow-local: ARIA snapshot equality for the structure class and difference for the text class on all six tasks
whether `--setting-sources project` loads `.claude/skills` of the cell project and nothing from the user's own settings (the init skill list answers it)

verify-config (offline apart from the official initializer, a local file-writing command): builds one real cell per arm and checks the CONTENT of what the loaded configuration produces: staged files, split-port transform, installed skills against the repository tree, argv per arm, call environment, scoring path; run it before the freeze

canary on the first cells of a run (preflight records first, then the first arm A and arm C cells of the drive): arm A must show, in one of its first three cells, completed generator_setup_page and generator_write_test calls and a parent playwright test run, and no cell may show an 'already used' port error, a denied generator or browser tool call or an infrastructure error (a cell where the model simply did not use the official tools is pending, not a failure); arm C must show the real skill invoked through the Skill tool without a Skill call error (a first cell with no executed preflight or exploration step is low model adherence, reported as a warning and never a failure, because fidelity is observed and not gated); modelUsage must cover the stream tokens
limits: 6 tasks x 2 repetitions per arm and model: tiny. The 6 tasks are the v1 synthetic fixtures with author-written faults.

Nothing about the real behaviour of the new transport was observed: the argv, the init contract, the port split and the prompts are tested offline against synthetic and stored v1 events only. The first live call may show a violation; the verifier then rejects it as an infrastructure error and the protocol is amended before the freeze.
The port split changes the generation project's app.mjs and config text (not their behaviour with the variable unset); the model reads those files. It is identical for all arms.
A project skill sits inside the worktree, which changes the skills' own trust classification of their scripts; the prompts grant the script commands explicitly (owner decision).

Arm A is the official subagent loop with a parent that cannot write files; arms B and C have Write and Edit. The asymmetry is intentional (mechanical enforcement that the generator writes the spec) and a confound with the arm effect.
Treatment status is a post-randomization variable; the as-treated and invoked views are per-protocol analyses and can be biased in either direction.

A background subagent can finish after the parent's first structured output, which produces a second init and result event; the harness uses the last result and checks every init, but the model's final status may then describe an unfinished child.
Arm B reviews the same model's own arm A output, so B and A cells are not independent; B fixes are written by a model that also wrote the code.
Claude runs on the host (real browser); Bash is not path-sandboxed (read denies plus an after-the-fact audit). Models run on different days and loads.
The classifier of the renamed-selector property is a string-literal heuristic; the secondary refactor edits are hand-written and statically checked only until validate-refactors has been run.

The authors read the stored v1 cells of claude-sonnet-5-5 (transcripts, scores) and the v1 protocol and harness before writing this protocol; they read no other Claude model's cells and no v1 summary.

Fidelity steps are counted from executed commands only (see fidelity.executed_vs_mentioned). The classifier cannot see a command hidden in a variable, a `for` list, an alias or a script the model wrote, so a step can be undercounted; it cannot be raised by text that merely mentions a script.

Arms B and C list Claude Code's bundled skills in their context and arm A lists none; the Skill allow rule restricts which skill may be invoked, not what is listed. Unintended Skill calls and denials are recorded per cell.

The edit lists of refactors.json were written after the authors had read the stored v1 sonnet specs and transcripts (not blind), and `validate-refactors` checks ARIA snapshots at the initial route only, so hidden or script-created nodes are not validated (see refactors.json validation_limits).
The renamed-selector reader was refined on the stored sonnet cells; its 8 of 8 and 25 of 25 are a reproduction on those cells, not a validation, and the split is true by construction.

Timed-out calls have only a lower-bound token record (streamed output counts are partial and USD is unknown); quality per token for an arm with timeouts is therefore optimistic by an unknown amount, and the timeout counts are printed beside it.

The campaign guard here lists v1, v2-codex and v2-claude runners and the verbs drive, run, preflight, init-check and harness-check by argument vector. The Codex runner's own guard is a separate file and does not list the Claude successor, so a Codex campaign can start while a Claude one runs unless both are aligned.

Running beside the Codex campaign shares CPU, memory and swap (swap was 88 percent used when this was written). The load pause at 40 is blind to that; host_pressure is recorded per cell and the cells started under pressure are not removed.

The Claude budget is account-wide: interactive use of the same plan counts against the same weekly window, so the operator stops the campaign at a utilization limit it reads from the CLI's rate-limit event.

power_simulation.purpose: offline Monte Carlo of the per-model sign rule, the family count rule and the pooled analysis for the four-model Claude roster
power_simulation.model: logit task effects shared by models, model effect sd 0.5, per-model effect heterogeneity sd 0.5, 2 repetitions, 6 tasks, ITT dilution (share of arm C cells that carry the effect)

coexistence.purpose: Run this Claude-family campaign at the same time as a Codex container campaign without sharing state, because the two spend different budgets.

true_conflicts.claude-family: another driver that spends the same Claude budget: this runner or the v1 runner (which runs Claude models); one Claude campaign at a time
true_conflicts.zeppelin: run-generator-oss-eval-v1, run-generator-thin-eval-v1 and run-generator-loop-v2 own the shared Zeppelin instance (fixed ports 14210 and 18080) and generator_oss_zeppelin.driver_processes pauses on ANY python run-generator-*.py with the verbs drive, run, preflight, score, smoke, harness-check, final-eval or calibrate, which includes this runner
true_conflicts.output-root: the same or a nested output root (flock on <output root>/.campaign.lock covers the same campaign; the guard also compares this root with every known driver's default root and with its readable environment override)
true_conflicts.ports: a known driver's host port hull overlapping this campaign's exact ranges, or a socket already listening inside them (lsof, best effort)
true_conflicts.unclassified: any other run-generator-*.py driver with a live verb: refused until it is classified in KNOWN_DRIVERS (fail closed)

not_conflicts.codex_container_drivers: run-generator-multimodel-v2-codex, v3-codex, v4-codex and the ablation driver: Codex runs inside a Colima container whose network namespace is its own, and their host-bound scoring ports use PORT_OFFSET 3000
not_conflicts.work_root: both runners stage under the same private work directory with distinct random names and neither sweeps it
not_conflicts.browser_cache: read-only for the host MCP browser and for scoring; neither campaign installs browsers
not_conflicts.campaign_locks: each runner takes a flock on its own output root

coexistence.shared_and_recorded_not_gated: CPU, memory and swap are shared with the Codex campaign and with the owner's other work. Every cell records host_pressure (1-minute load, swap used and total) beside load_at_start; the inherited load pause and flag at 40 apply unchanged.
coexistence.port_ranges: exact for the full 36-cell schedule: scoring 11301-11948, generation 12301-12372, preflight and init-check 12701-12706, secondary scoring 13301-13444, validate-refactors 14301-14342, and the MCP app server of arm A at the generation and preflight ports plus 20000 (32301-32372 and 32701-32706); all below the ephemeral range. The Codex v3 campaign's ranges for its 72-cell schedule are 8301-9596 (scoring, host-bound), 9301-9444 and 9701-9712 (inside its container). The offline test derives both sets from the sources and the protocols and asserts they are disjoint.

machine_wide_probes.codex_runners: the pgrep patterns of the Codex v2, v3, v4 and thin-integration runners (`run-generator-multimodel-v[123](-codex)?\.py (drive|...)`) do not match this runner's name, so a Codex driver neither pauses nor refuses because of this campaign
machine_wide_probes.zeppelin_helper: its driver_processes() does match this runner (see zeppelin above)
machine_wide_probes.previous_guard: the previous guard of this runner matched only v1, v2-codex and v2-claude and could not see the v3 or v4 Codex drivers at all

coexistence.verbs: guard (read-only report), status, verify-config, canary: offline, no model call
